one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-08) should contain Corning's Q3 2026 report. The date is not confirmed by Corning; Q3 2025 was reported Oct 28, so late October is expected. Guidance is core sales $4.9-5.0B and core EPS $0.85-0.89 [1]. Hyperscaler Q3 reports with 2027 capex commentary, and Prysmian/Fujikura/Lumentum updates, also fall in the window. Value-chain reads into the print are positive: Amphenol book-to-bill 1.23 [12], Lumentum's strong FQ4 and guide [11], and fibre makers' profits multiplying on tight preform supply [6,9,10,13]. But all four of the last release-day reactions were negative on Twelve Data closes [4]: Oct 28, 2025 -3.3%, Jan 28, 2026 -5.0%, Apr 28, 2026 -8.9%, and Jul 28, 2026 -12.1% (143.36 to 126.01; I wrongly said -19% in round 1). Four points are too few to be a strong signal, so I tilt the centre only about 1% below spot (median $155.5). Realized vol is about 77% over the last 63 trading days and 69% over the last 40 [4], giving a monthly sigma of 0.69/3.5 = about 20%. I use a mixture of 70% at sigma 0.17 and 30% at sigma 0.25 to capture the earnings-day fat tail.

fair_value.method: Estimate: 70% P/E (26.5x x Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.13 = $135.9) + 30% Springboard cross-check ($30B end-2028 run-rate x 16.6% net margin / 888M shares = $5.61 x 26.5x = $148.7, discounted 1.17 yrs at 10% = $133.0). 0.7 x 135.9 + 0.3 x 133.0 = $135.1, rounded to $135. The 26.5x is the 28.1x consistent-basis peer median less 1.6x for GLW-specific risks after the horizon (see long_dated_risks). Core EPS already bears stock-based compensation.

inputs_detail.derivation: SBC check: Corning's core EPS does NOT add back stock-based compensation. The Q2 2026 GAAP-to-core reconciliation [1] has no SBC line: GAAP $0.64 to core $0.78 via hedged exposures, translated-earnings contract, acquisition costs, tax, restructuring, pension and investments. SBC was $135M in Q2 and $250M in H1 per the cash-flow statement [1]. So the EPS I capitalise is already net of SBC. I do not also count SBC share issuance as dilution: that would double count, and core diluted shares (875M) already include dilutive awards.

4.37 x 1.25 x 0.985 = 5.38. The +25% assumes about half the operating leverage consensus has in FY27 (EPS +33% on revenue +19.6% [3]). The 0.985 is dilution from the full $2.0B ATM [5]: 2,000 / 156.68 = 12.8M shares on 875M core diluted shares [1] = 1.46%.
0.25 x 4.37 + 0.75 x 5.38 = 5.13 (the Oct-2027 NTM covers about Q4'27 plus Q1-Q3'28).

Consistent-basis peer median: price / calendarised consensus NTM EPS for 11 peers, giving 28.1x (TEL 16.8 ... ANET 43.8). Long-dated risk adjustment: the probability-weighted, GLW-specific post-horizon effects I build into the multiple total -$8.6/share (fibre capacity and price normalisation -4.0, Glass Innovations -1.7, contract re-pricing -1.3, further equity -0.9, hollow-core content -0.7; see long_dated_risks). 8.6 / 5.13 = 1.7x, so 28.1 - 1.7 = 26.4x, rounded to 26.5x. AI-capex cyclicality is shared by every peer, so it is already in the median and gets no extra cut. SBC basis: peer consensus EPS is 'non-GAAP adjusted', and at least Lumentum adds back SBC (verified: $50.1M in FQ4'26 [11]). On an SBC-burdened basis such peers' multiples would be higher, so applying an adjusted-basis median to Corning's SBC-burdened core EPS is conservative. I verified only LITE's treatment, and LITE is already above the median, so the median is left unchanged rather than raised on unverified assumptions.

Same 26.5x as the P/E method (28.1x peer median less 1.7x long-dated GLW-specific risk).

bear.story: AI optical spend digests in 2027-28 while announced capacity lands: Corning plans +50% and Prysmian 2x US fibre capacity [7], competitors restart preform capacity [6], and fibre makers flush with record profits [9,10,13] add supply. Fibre prices that rose 80%+ in China [6] normalise, and the Meta contract runs at the low end of 'up to' [8]. Buyers in Oct 2027 then price several years of post-horizon price and volume pressure. FY2028 EPS is about $4.6 and the multiple de-rates to about 20.6x (CLS/PRY end of the peer set): 4.6 x 20.6 = $95. The probability is raised to 27% because the reverse DCF shows even the peer multiple needs mid-teens EPS growth for nine years after the horizon.

base.story: Springboard stays on track ($20B run-rate end-2026, heading for $30B end-2028 [1]). Optical keeps growing 25-30% while Glass/Auto stay flat. NTM EPS reaches about $5.13, and the multiple converges only partway from 38.2x today toward my 26.5x risk-adjusted fair multiple: 5.13 x 28x = $144.

bull.story: Fibre tightness persists through 2027. Preform is the upstream bottleneck [6,7], Amphenol and Lumentum results show strong AI demand [11,12], and Corning's CPO fiber-to-chip products [40] widen content. Corning beats Springboard and lifts its 2028 targets, so Oct-2027 NTM EPS is about $5.8. The market pays 36x, just below today's 38.2x, because post-2028 capacity additions [7] cap enthusiasm: 5.8 x 36 = $209, about $210. That is still below the record close of $255.69 on Jun 29, 2026 [4].

comps_summary.peer_range: Consistent-basis NTM P/E runs from 16.8x (TEL) to 43.8x (ANET) across the 11 rebased peers, median 28.1x. Next-year EPS growth runs from 13% (TEL) to 75% (CLS), median about 36%. No forward EV/EBITDA is available at source, so no EV/EBITDA median is given and no EV/EBITDA method is used.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 26.5x, 1.6x below the 28.1x consistent-basis median and inside the peer range (16.8x-43.8x). GLW trades at 38.2x on the same basis (156.68 / $4.10). The discount is the probability-weighted, GLW-specific post-horizon risk in long_dated_risks (-$8.6/share). Basis note: GLW core EPS is SBC-burdened [1], while at least some peers' adjusted EPS excludes SBC (LITE verified [11]), so the comparison is conservative.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. GLW's FY2027 consensus EPS growth (+33% [3]) is at or below the peer median (~36%). About 47% of Q2 core sales grew -15% to +2% [1], and growth is partly equity-funded ($2B ATM [5]). Small discount (1.6x): unlike most of the AI-infrastructure peer set, a large share of GLW's optical profit is in fibre and cable, a capacity-cyclical product where Corning itself (+50%) and Prysmian (2x) are expanding US capacity [7]. Chinese prices already swung from a mid-2025 tender slump to +80% [6,7], and new capacity 'may moderate price pressure over time' [7]. Hollow-core and multicore fibre could lower fibre-km per bit after 2029 [39,40]. Glass Innovations growth is flat (+1% in Q2 [1]). These risks land mostly after Oct 2027 but are paid for by a buyer at the horizon, so they are in the multiple. Only Prysmian (21.2x) in the peer median shares the fibre-cycle exposure, which is why I count most of that risk as incremental to the median.

thesis_break_reason: $100 is about 22.9x consensus FY2027 EPS of $4.37 [3] and 13% below the Jul 28, 2026 post-earnings intraday low of $114.50 [4]. GLW last closed near $100 in late January 2026, before the Meta deal re-rating [4]. Trading there would most likely mean the market believes the AI fibre demand or pricing cycle has turned (hyperscaler capex cuts, fibre price roll-over as new capacity [7] arrives) or that consensus 2027 EPS is being cut, rather than ordinary noise at 70% volatility.

reasoning: Lane: industry/value chain. Facts from the Q2 8-K [1]: core sales $4.74B (+17%), core EPS $0.78 (+30%), Optical $2.07B (+32%), Glass Innovations +1%, Auto +2%, Life Sciences -15%; Q3 guide $0.85-0.89; Springboard $20B/$30B/$40B run-rates. The chain confirms strong demand: CRU (Chinese fibre +80% Nov-25 to Jan-26, preform the bottleneck) [6], YOFC [13], Fujikura [10], Prysmian [9], Amphenol [12] and Lumentum [11]. The chain also confirms new supply: Hengtong notes price rises are uneven by region, that data centers were only about 5% of 2025 optical cable demand, and that Corning (+50%) and Prysmian (2x) are expanding US fibre capacity [7]. That is context for the scenarios, not a number. Round-2 changes: (1) The supervisor showed the StockAnalysis 'forward P/E' uses lagged or current-FY EPS. I verified this myself by opening 11 peer forecast pages and rebuilding NTM multiples; the median is 28.1x, not 29.5x. (2) I opened the ATM 8-K [5] and applied about 1.5% dilution, so NTM EPS is $5.13, not $5.19. (3) Price-history errors are fixed from Twelve Data [4]: July release day -12.1%, not -19%; $271.78 was an intraday high, and the record close was $255.69. (4) The 'Lumentum capacity committed into 2029' claim and its Finviz source are removed from everything. Post-horizon risks (method change of 2026-10-12): fibre capacity and price normalisation, AI-capex digestion, hollow-core content, contract re-pricing, further equity and Glass weakness. They are quantified in long_dated_risks; the GLW-specific -$8.6/share takes the multiple from 28.1x to 26.5x. The reverse DCF shows 26.5x still needs ~14.6% EPS growth for nine years after the horizon at a 10% cost of equity. SBC check: core EPS does not add back SBC ($135M in Q2) [1], so the capitalised EPS is SBC-burdened. Peers' adjusted EPS (e.g. LITE [11]) adds it back, so the comparison is conservative and left unadjusted. Fair value is $135 (P/E $135.9, Springboard $133.0). Distribution: I do not assume full multiple convergence in 12 months, so I centre the median at $142, between fair value and spot. Scenarios: bear $95 (27%), base $144 (50%), bull $210 (23%). The ladder is a lognormal mixture (60% at sigma 0.42, 40% at sigma 0.68) for the fat tails seen in a stock with a $78-$256 closing range over the past year [4]. Research limits: FY2028 peer EPS is Pro-gated on some pages, so 'EPS next year' summary values were used where shown; there is no forward EV/EBITDA at source.

long_dated_risks.risk: Fibre capacity additions (Corning +50% US, Prysmian 2x US, Chinese preform restarts) leading to optical-fibre price normalisation
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Fibre/cable prices -15% on roughly half of Optical sales (judgment: fibre and cable vs connectivity hardware), so Optical revenue -7.5%. At 44% of sales [1] and high decremental margins, group core EPS is about -8% from 2028-29 onward versus base.
long_dated_risks.how_applied: multiple: 0.5 x 8% x $143.6 = -$5.7 gross. I apply -$4.0 into the multiple, treating the rest as already priced through Prysmian and other cyclical names in the peer median. Also drives the bear scenario.

long_dated_risks.risk: Hyperscaler AI capex slowdown or digestion after the 2026-27 build
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Enterprise/hyperscale Optical volumes fall. Group core EPS about -15% for 2-3 years versus base (judgment from Optical at 44% of sales [1], with enterprise the fastest-growing part).
long_dated_risks.how_applied: multiple: 0.35 x 15% x $143.6 = -$7.5 gross. No extra cut, because every peer in the median (LITE, CIEN, ANET, CRDO, VRT, CLS) shares and is more exposed to this risk, so it is already in the 28.1x. It is the main driver of the bear scenario (27%).

long_dated_risks.risk: Hollow-core and multicore fibre lowering conventional fibre-km per bit; competing HCF suppliers (Microsoft/Lumenisity, Heraeus, others)
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Optical revenue -5% from about 2030 if conventional single-mode volumes per unit of bandwidth fall and Corning does not hold share in HCF. This is partly hedged: Corning is one of Microsoft's two named HCF production partners [39] and sells multicore fibre with 4x capacity per fibre [40]. Group EPS about -2.5%.

long_dated_risks.risk: Co-packaged optics bringing fibre to the chip (upside content shift)
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: More fibre and connectivity per switch/GPU (Corning shows CPO fiber-to-chip connectors and trays [40]). The trade-press per-GPU content multipliers could not be confirmed at source, so no amount is quantified.

long_dated_risks.risk: Customer long-term agreements (e.g. Meta, 'multiyear', up to $6B) re-pricing or not renewing when they expire. The ~2029 expiry date is not disclosed (the source says only 'multiyear'), so timing is uncertain.

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Another ~$2B raise at ~$150 adds about 13M shares, 1.5% dilution to EPS per share.
long_dated_risks.how_applied: multiple: 0.4 x 1.5% x $143.6 = -$0.9 (the current ATM is already in the share count)

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Glass Innovations grew only +1% in Q2 [1]. If its profit declines about 5% a year after 2027 instead of staying flat, group EPS is about -3% by 2030.

reverse_dcf_check: At the horizon, 26.5x x $5.13 = $135.9. I reverse that with a 10% cost of equity, FCF conversion of core net income rising from 75% to 90% over 10 years, and 3% terminal growth. The Q2 2026 ex-deposit conversion was (1,423 - 880) / 680 = 80% [1]; 75% allows for heavy expansion capex. On those inputs the price implies about 14.6% a year core EPS growth for 2029-2037, i.e. EPS about $17.4 by year 10, with core net margin held around 16.6-18%. The peer median 28x would need 15.4%. Plausibility check against the evidence: Springboard's 19% sales CAGR from Q4'26 to Q4'30 [1] supports about 20% EPS growth in 2029-30. If growth then fades linearly from 15% to 3%, the DCF gives only about $115 at 10%; that path justifies 26.5x only at about a 9.0% cost of equity. So even my risk-adjusted multiple assumes Springboard is delivered and growth stays double-digit into the 2030s, despite the capacity, price, technology and Glass risks above. I keep the peer-relative multiple because AI-infrastructure peers are priced on the same implied discount rate, but the gap is why I apply no premium, take a 1.6x long-dated discount, and keep a fat 27% bear tail. The SBC-burdened core EPS [1] makes the implied growth slightly less demanding than it would be on an SBC-excluded basis.
